added: **Applies to:** All projects. This file is the core, which every repository loads; the files
under `rules/` are loaded only where they apply (§SCOPE).
**Master copy:** `standards/project-rules.md` and `standards/rules/` in
`github.com/Tanveerfb/fleet-standards`. One version covers the set.
**The standard is a set of files, split by concern.** Every repository loads this file, the
core. The rest are loaded only where they apply:
| File | Concern | Loaded by |
| `project-rules.md` | How we work (the core) | Every repository |
| `rules/app.md` | Engineering, in any language | Anything with application code |
| `rules/ui.md` | Interface | Anything with a visual surface |
| `rules/node.md` | The Node and TypeScript stack | Web projects and Node tools |
| `rules/web.md` | The Next.js stack | Web projects |
| `rules/game.md` | The game-engine stack | Games |
| `rules/non-application.md` | What a repository without application code does differently | Those repositories |
| `rules/options/credit.md`, `trello.md`, `firebase.md` | Things a project opts into at setup | Projects that chose them |
| `rules/options/ai.md` | AI and model features | Read on demand by projects that chose it |
| Kind of repository | Loads |
| Web project (Next.js) | core, app, ui, node, web, its options |
| Local Node tool | core, app, node; ui if it has an interface; its options |
| Tool in another language (bash, Python) | core, app; ui if it has an interface |
| Game | core, app, ui, game, its options |
| Non-application | core, non-application; ui if it has a visual surface |
**A project declares what it loads** in its `CLAUDE.md`: one import line per file, and one
line beside *Deploys* that `sync-standards` reads:
`Rules: app, ui, node, web · Options: firebase, trello`. Sync copies and updates only the
files declared. A section that divides between files keeps its name in each.
**The options are asked about once.** `new-project` and `sync-standards` ask about each —
the studio credit, a Trello board, Firebase, AI — and record the answer, so a project that
never opted in has still been asked.
One file of the fleet standard. `project-rules.md` is the core: its §SCOPE lists every file in
the set and who loads it, and its header carries the one version they share.
# Fleet rules — engineering (`rules/app.md`)
**Loaded by:** anything with application code.
# Fleet rules — interface (`rules/ui.md`)
**Loaded by:** anything with a visual surface.
# Fleet rules — the Node and TypeScript stack (`rules/node.md`)
**Loaded by:** web projects and Node tools.
# Fleet rules — the Next.js stack (`rules/web.md`)
**Loaded by:** web projects.
# Fleet rules — the game-engine stack (`rules/game.md`)
**Loaded by:** games built in an engine.
# Fleet rules — repositories without application code (`rules/non-application.md`)
**Loaded by:** repositories without application code.
# Fleet rules — option: studio credit (`rules/options/credit.md`)
# Fleet rules — option: Trello (`rules/options/trello.md`)
# Fleet rules — option: Firebase (`rules/options/firebase.md`)
**Loaded by:** projects that chose it at setup.
# Fleet rules — option: AI and model features (`rules/options/ai.md`)
**Loaded by:** nothing by default. Read on demand, by projects that chose it.
[`motifs.md`](../motifs.md) in the master copy of this standard.
- **The core**, `project-rules.md`, in full
- **`rules/ui.md`**, imported wherever the work has a visual surface (pages, navigation,
forms on the platform)
Nothing else under `rules/` applies. If application code later lands in the repository, it
loads the files for that code from that day (§SCOPE). These things read differently here:
## §NAMING — Naming
## §MOTION — Motion
## §BUILD — Comments, cleanliness and build discipline
## §TESTING — Testing
*§NAMING continues in `rules/node.md`: file and identifier case.*
*§NAMING's vocabulary rules are in `rules/app.md`.*
*§MOTION continues in `rules/web.md`: the library.*
*§MOTION's rules are in `rules/ui.md`.*
*§BUILD continues in `rules/node.md`: the typecheck, lint and build commands.*
*§BUILD's rules on comments, leftovers and failing builds are in `rules/app.md`.*
*§TESTING continues in `rules/node.md` (unit tests) and `rules/web.md` (the browser check).*
*§TESTING's universal rules are in the core, `project-rules.md`; the browser check is in `rules/web.md`.*
*§TESTING's universal rules are in the core, `project-rules.md`; unit tests are in `rules/node.md`.*
